subject: Request: Service commitment exception & order form amendments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@greenriverdx.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@greenriverdx.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: service commitment exception & order form amendments

Emma / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Following up with a formal ask so we have a single record for legal and procurement. GreenRiver is requesting two changes to our standard order form / MSA package before procurement can sign:

1) Availability appendix: customer is asking for a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment for production inference endpoints (all models serving customer data). They want the definition spelled out and credits tied to monthly unavailability.
2) Latency SLOs: a P95 latency target for short-text generation endpoints and a P99 target for long-sequence workloads. They want these included in the order form rather than an internal SLO table.

We generally can accept an availability appendix but need to define the maintenance window exclusions, SLA measurement window, and liability/credit language. I attached our proposed redline to the General MSA and an initial order form draft (Attachment: GreenRiver_General_MSA_redline.pdf; OrderForm_UptimeAppendix_v2.docx). Also attaching our operational evidence export for the past 12 months so procurement can validate baseline availability (Attachment: evidence-uptime-logs-2025-2026.zip).

Questions for procurement:
- Is GreenRiver comfortable with credits as a percentage-of-monthly-fees cap (we typically cap at 30% per month, cumulative cap per incident)?
- Would they accept P95/P99 targets expressed as percentiles over a calendar month measured at the API gateway?

If procurement can confirm the acceptable credit cap and any special carve-outs (e.g., third-party network outages), I’ll loop in Legal (soojin_lee) and Engineering (karthik_iyer) to finalize wording.

Next steps: please confirm timeline for legal review and whether you need additional operational evidence.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: GreenRiver_General_MSA_redline.pdf (redline PDF)
Attachment: OrderForm_UptimeAppendix_v2.docx (draft order form)
Attachment: evidence-uptime-logs-2025-2026.zip (ops export)

Subject: Re: Request: service commitment exception & order form amendments

Ben —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the artifacts. We reviewed the attachments and have a few note-level items from procurement and IT security:

- Availability: procurement prefers a 99.9% monthly target in contract language with a clearly defined credit schedule. They want to avoid language that guarantees >99.95% without uptime evidence. Can you provide a short summary of your historical monthly uptime distribution? The evidence zip is helpful — we’ll need an executive summary we can share internally.
- Credits: the finance team prefers credits tied to % of monthly invoice, with an aggregate cap of 50% of the monthly spend over the month of the breach. Can Redwood accept that (or propose your maximum)?
- Maintenance windows: we need precise advance notice for scheduled maintenance and a max duration per month that is excluded from uptime calculations.
- Latency: IT asks that P95 for short text be ≤ 300ms and P99 for long sequences ≤ 800ms as aspirational SLOs. We understand these may differ by model family; procurement requests example routes/endpoints and an explanation for any model-specific variance.

We’re open to the Availability Appendix as an addendum to the order form, but procurement requires a single consolidated doc for legal review. I’m attaching GreenRiver’s vendor SLA template for reference (Attachment: GreenRiver_VendorSLA_Template.pdf).

Can you get Legal and Engineering to propose final text for the order form appendix that maps to our asks? Also confirm whether Redwood is willing to offer dedicated capacity / reserved pool options (we may pursue a Dedicated SKU if it helps with the latency/availability guarantees).

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: service commitment exception & order form amendments

Soojin / Karthik —

Forwarding GreenRiver’s reply (below). Procurement is pushing back on the 99.95% ask and wants 99.9% + a credit schedule. Finance is asking for a higher aggregate credit cap (50% monthly) which is above our standard. They also asked for specific P95/P99 latency thresholds by endpoint.

Quick notes from my side and asks:
- Engineering: can you confirm whether we can commit to the P95/P99 thresholds as measured at the API gateway for the long-tail model families? If not, we should provide per-model families or a carve-out for long-sequence transforms. Also advise what Dedicated capacity level (reserved GPU pool) would be required to make 99.95%/P95=200ms realistic.
- Legal: we need a proposed order-form appendix that: defines uptime measurement, scheduled maintenance exclusion (48 hours notice, max 4 hours/month exclusion), credit schedule, and a liability cap consistent with our standard (propose monthly-credit cap = 30% and annual aggregate cap = 150% of monthly fees). Please review GreenRiver’s template (procurement attached) and our redlines (attached here).

I attached the redline + a cleaned order form I drafted: OrderForm_UptimeAppendix_v2.docx (edited), GreenRiver_General_MSA_redline.pdf (uploaded), evidence-uptime-logs-2025-2026.zip (ops export).

If Legal and Eng can give a short set of proposed contract bullets today, I’ll push back to procurement with specific options (e.g., 99.9% standard + an optional Dedicated SKU for 99.95%).

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_UptimeAppendix_v2.docx
Attachment: GreenRiver_General_MSA_redline.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: service commitment exception & order form amendments

Ben —

Thanks for the thread and the attachments. I reviewed the proposed appendix and GreenRiver’s vendor template. High-level takeaways:

- We can offer an Availability Appendix; recommend default contract language at 99.9% monthly uptime with an optional upgrade to 99.95% if the customer commits to a Dedicated reserved pool (we’ll tie this to a minimum monthly committed spend).
- Credits: counter-propose a monthly incident credit schedule and cap the monthly credits at 30% of the affected services’ monthly invoice, with an annual aggregate cap of 150% of monthly fees (this keeps our exposure bounded while providing meaningful remediation).
- Maintenance exclusion: propose 72 hours advance notice for planned maintenance that impacts uptime (we are willing to negotiate down to 48 hours for major customers but prefer 72 hrs as default); exclude up to 4 hours/month from availability measurement, beyond that credits apply.
- Liability: standard liability cap applies; avoid any unlimited liability language.

I’ve attached a small edit to your OrderForm_UptimeAppendix_v2.docx with the proposed credit language and the Dedicated upgrade option. If this looks good to Engineering, Ben — please send to procurement with a short cover note offering two options (A: 99.9% base with our credit schedule; B: 99.95% with Dedicated commitment and pre-agreed monthly spend). We can prepare the DocuSign envelope once procurement confirms which option they prefer.
